yt.title: Spain's economy was 52% of Italy's in 2000. Now? #Shorts
yt.description:
GDP in current US dollars, Spain as a share of Italy, 2000 vs 2025. Source: World Bank (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD). Both countries use the euro, so the dollar exchange rate largely cancels out of this ratio.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.narration: Spain and Italy are two of the biggest economies in southern Europe. Here is how the gap between them changed.
In 2000, Spain's economy was fifty-two percent the size of Italy's. By 2025, it was seventy-five percent.
Both countries use the euro, so the exchange rate barely moves this ratio. Spain's economy simply grew faster. What would you compare next?
